prompt:
Paint ONE building for a top-down pixel-art JRPG town map, in the classic 3/4 top-down RPG view: the roof is seen from above (it fills the upper coloured block of the guide) and the front wall is seen straight on (the lower block). The attached image is an exact layout guide drawn at the final proportions: keep the outer silhouette, the roof/wall split line, the door (dark brown rectangle: it must stay exactly there, same size, at ground level, a real door you can walk through) and the windows (yellow rectangles) in exactly the same places. You may add small details (eaves, trim, drainpipe, flower boxes, crates by the wall, a chimney poking above the roof into the empty top margin).
This building: a one-storey house in a forest village built among giant trees (rustic log houses, carved wood, lanterns). thick golden-brown straw thatch roof walls of stacked round logs with notched corners. Windows have small panes glowing warm amber from inside (the only light). The whole image is 208 x 160 art pixels (each art pixel 7x7 image pixels).
Premium modern hi-bit 2D pixel art ("HD pixel art" JRPG look), hand-placed pixels. Every art pixel is a crisp square of the same size across the whole image (about 8x8 image pixels per art pixel). No anti-aliasing, no blur, no soft brushes, no photographic texture, no noise, no dithering checkerboards. Clusters of 3-10 pixels with clear shapes. Hue-shifted colour ramps: shadows lean toward purple/red and are more saturated, highlights lean toward warm yellow. 4-6 shades per material, rich but earthy, worn and lived-in.
Lighting: neutral, soft, even light from the upper left, like a calm overcast evening; NO cast shadows, NO night darkness, NO lamp light pools, NO vignette. (The game engine adds the night lighting on top later, so this must be the clean base colours.)
Background: fully transparent (the magenta in the guide is background). No ground, no shadow, no people, no text, no letters.
revised_prompt: Edit the ATTACHED layout guide into ONE isolated pixel-art forest-village log house, using the guide as a strict positional mask and composition. Canvas exactly 1456 x 1120 pixels representing 208 x 160 art pixels, square pixel grid 7x7 physical pixels, hard sharp grid-aligned edges, transparent alpha background where guide is magenta. The roof outer silhouette remains precisely x14–1443, y196–714 physical pixels, with horizontal division around y423–437 between the top-down roof surface and front-facing thick thatch eave. Roof occupies the upper block; straight-on front wall occupies lower block, x56–1400, y715–1119. The two glowing window openings MUST remain in their exact guide locations and sizes (left x392–505 y896–1037, right x938–1051 y896–1037); maintain recognizable warm amber glass with tiny dark wooden mullions and frames. Preserve the guide's dark-brown ground-level door exactly in place and exactly the same size if visible in source; it is an actual walk-through door, NOT a window, do not change or relocate it. Do not invent extra windows or change building proportions. This is a rustic one-story house built among giant forest trees: lush thick golden-brown straw thatch roof with beautiful discrete 3–10-art-pixel clumps of straw, a substantial dark-golden eave; stacked horizontal ROUND wooden logs on front wall, with carved grain, dark notched end corners and timber structural details. Warm amber glowing window panes are the ONLY emitting lights. Neutral even soft upper-left overcast light; clean well-lit base colors, no cast shadow, no nighttime filter, no external lights. Premium modern HD pixel-art JRPG sprite quality, beautiful considered hand-placed opaque color clusters, warm yellow highlights and richer purple/red shadows, four to six carefully chosen shades per material, earthy and inviting lived-in look. Absolutely no antialiasing, smoothing, blur, semitransparency, pixel noise, photographic textures, or checkerboard dithering. No scene, ground, shadows, figures, text, lettering, or magenta background: fully transparent outside building. Stay faithful to reference layout, roof/wall horizontal boundaries, and position of all openings.
